title: Automotive Axles (AUTOAXLES) - LIVE deep dive #3, first cheap-tercile draw (protocol v1.3 stages 2-7): method test, no verdict; card size 0; 6 live calls
body: LIVE method test (L9, L21): random draw from the cheapest EV/EBITDA tercile of a 120-name random sample of the India non-financial Rs 1,000-20,000 cr universe; no buy/sell verdict. Research, not advice. SELECTION: 809 in range -> 741 eligible -> sample 120 (Random(20261125)) -> 111 valid -> cheapest tercile 37 (EV/EBITDA <= 11.86x) -> Random(20261126) walk: JPPOWER skipped (PEAD Q1, event 19-Oct-2026), AUTOAXLES passed all v3 checks (pledge 0, unmodified audits, PEAD Q5 SUE +4.19, solvency 0 flags). WHY CHEAP: cyclical peak, not fraud or solvency. P/E 12.9x trailing (record EPS 137.6 adj; record OPM 12.5% in Q2 FY27) vs 25.8x on 10-year normalised EPS 68.9; FY26 M&HCV industry ~480k = FY19 peak; FY27 guided 500k+ with a regulatory pre-buy to April 2027; capacity ~98% used; last cycle revenue -53%, EPS -81%, price -80% (2018-20). KEY FINDINGS: (1) since 1-Apr-2025 AAL sells direct to OEMs and pays Meritor HVS (India) (Cummins) a technical fee, Rs 97.5 cr FY26 = 4.5% of sales = 41% of core EBITDA, under a one-year agreement renewable 30-Apr-2027, after minorities rejected a Rs 2,500 cr material-RPT resolution 79.5% against (Dec-2024); (2) the switch grossed revenue up ~5% (materials 71.0% -> 67.5% of revenue), so FY26 like-for-like revenue was ~flat vs industry +16%; (3) Customer A = 66% of revenue; (4) net cash Rs 394 cr (15% of mcap), ICRA AA-, ROIC 15-22% FY23-26; (5) promise ledger 43% vs auto-peer median 60%: dates slip, industry forecasts too bearish twice. VALUATION: worksheet v1.3 EV 1.49x raw / 1.40x anchored (w=0.6) vs hurdle 1.76x -> card v1.2 size 0; base IRR 10.4%; exit-bet table 1.13x (DCF P/E) / 1.49x / 1.73x (own median 18.8). METHOD LESSONS: cheap tercile selects cycle position; materials-ratio test for sales-model gross-ups; minority vote results are governance data.

title: Automotive Axles (AUTOAXLES) variant view, Nov 2026: cheap for a reason (cyclical peak + parent fee); no claimable mispricing
body: Market appears to price peak M&HCV earnings that fall after the April-2027 pre-buy (12.9x trailing, ~26x normalised). Our view: agree on direction; no claimable mispricing. We add two negatives the market may under-weight - FY26 like-for-like revenue ~flat vs industry +16% (direct-sales gross-up) and an annually renewed 4.5%-of-sales technical fee to the Cummins group that minorities cannot vote on - and one positive: net cash 15% of mcap and through-cycle ROIC ~15%, so the left tail is a cyclical drawdown, not ruin. Proves us wrong: FY27 revenue >= Rs 2,500 cr AND H1 FY28 revenue within 10% of H1 FY27; fee stable on a multi-year agreement; FY27 growth >= industry + 5 pts. Scored by thesis:paper-call:AUTOAXLES:*.

title: Decision card AUTOAXLES 2026-11-23 (paper)
body: Decision card v1 for Automotive Axles Ltd. Rule output: size 0: blocked by Expected value vs hurdle (EV 1.40x anchored (raw 1.49x) vs hurdle 1.76x → below hurdle → size 0). Thesis: Method-test thesis: Automotive Axles is cheap only on peak-cycle earnings (12.9x trailing, 25.8x 10-year normalised EPS); over 5 years it compounds roughly with the M&HCV cycle at a through-cycle ROIC ~15-18% while its parent (Cummins/Meritor) takes ~4.5% of sales as a technical fee under an annually renewed agreement, so the 5-year outcome is driven by cycle position in FY31-32 and the exit multiple, not by a mispricing. Variant view: Market (reverse DCF and temperature): at Rs 1,776 the stock is at 12.9x trailing EPS, 8.1x EV/EBITDA net of Rs 394 cr cash, the lowest P/E on the highest earnings in its 11-year history; the market is pricing a cyclical peak (record FY27 M&HCV volume of 500k+ guided, a regulatory pre-buy to April 2027, capacity nearly full at a Rs 2,650 cr annualised run-rate). Our view: we largely AGREE that it is cheap for a reason, so there is no claimable mispricing. On 10-year normalised EPS (Rs 69) the P/E is 25.8x (warm vs own history); the last cycle took revenue -53% and EPS -81% (FY19-21) and the price -80% peak to trough. What we found that the market may be MIS-weighting, in both directions: (1, negative) like-for-like FY26 revenue was roughly flat while the industry grew ~16% - the reported +4.8% is mostly the gross-up from selling direct to OEMs at OEM prices since 1-Apr-2025 (materials fell 71.0% -> 67.5% of revenue, other expenses rose 11.7% -> 14.3% with the new Rs 97.5 cr technical fee) - so content/share per industry vehicle has lagged; (2, negative) the parent take is now an explicit 4.5%-of-sales fee to Meritor HVS India (Cummins) under a one-year agreement renewable 30-Apr-2027, structured below the shareholder-approval threshold after minority holders voted 79.5% against a Rs 2,500 cr material-RPT resolution in Dec-2024; (3, positive) the balance sheet is clean (net cash 15% of market cap, AA- ICRA, payout ~30%) and the business earned 15-22% ROIC across FY23-26, so the downside is a cyclical drawdown, not a solvency event. What would prove us wrong: FY27 revenue >= Rs 2,500 cr AND FY28 H1 revenue holding within 10% of H1 FY27 after the pre-buy (the cycle is longer than we assume), or a fee cut/stable fee with rising content per vehicle. Departure from the outside view: P(>=3x) far below the class (6% vs 21%) because a 3x needs ~25% EPS CAGR from a cyclical-peak base (twin engine); tail probabilities are anchored at w=0.6 toward the class because this stock already printed a ~0.2x drawdown in the last cycle. Checked by paper calls thesis:paper-call:AUTOAXLES:* (6 operating/fee/price calls to 2027-09-30, plus the 3 card calls). Open soft flags: 5. P(≥3x) 6% vs base 21%; P(≤0.5x) 4% vs base 11.3%; EV 5-yr multiple 1.49x vs hurdle 1.76x. Review 2027-02-15.

title: When a related-party sales channel is removed, re-derive like-for-like growth from the materials ratio before trusting reported growth
body: Technique (AUTOAXLES, live deep dive #3, Nov 2026): AAL stopped selling ~80% of output through Meritor HVS (India) and began selling direct to OEMs at OEM prices from 1-Apr-2025, paying a technical fee instead. Materials fell from 71.0% to 67.5% of revenue and other expenses rose from 11.7% to 14.3%, so ~5% of FY26's +4.8% revenue growth was price gross-up, not volume: like-for-like revenue was ~flat while the M&HCV industry grew ~16%. Rule: when the customer of record changes (distributor/parent -> end customer), compute gross-up = old materials ratio / new materials ratio and deflate growth by it; check that OPM moved little (it should if the change is arm's length).

title: A 'cheapest EV/EBITDA tercile' draw tends to select cyclicals at peak earnings: read the valuation on normalised EPS as well as trailing
body: First cheap-tercile live draw (AUTOAXLES, 23-Nov-2026): trailing P/E 12.9x read COLD (0th percentile of own history) while P/E on 10-year normalised EPS read WARM (25.8x, 70th percentile). The stock had looked similarly 'cheap' at the FY19 peak (16x) and then fell 80%. Value-trap test order for any cheap draw: (1) is EPS at a cycle or margin peak (compare with 10-year mean EPS and prior-peak OPM)? (2) is a turn dated (pre-buy, regulation, capacity full)? (3) capital allocation and parent take; (4) fraud/solvency. Single case (n=1); scored by the AUTOAXLES live calls and card calls.

title: Automotive Axles minority shareholders reject Rs 2,500 cr material RPT with Meritor HVS (India), 14-Dec-2024 (79.47% against)
body: Postal ballot (ordinary resolution) to approve FY26 material related-party transactions of Rs 25,000 mn with Meritor HVS (India) Ltd was rejected: 20.53% for, 79.47% against (related parties cannot vote). The board then (20/31-Mar-2025) signed an MoU and a services agreement: AAL sells direct to OEMs from 1-Apr-2025 and pays MHVSIL a technical fee (Rs 97.5 cr FY26), extended on 29-Apr-2026 to 30-Apr-2027.
